subject: physics
chapter_title: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

concepts.title: Work Function
concepts.definition: The smallest quantity of energy an electron needs to absorb to successfully break free from the surface of a specific metal.
concepts.key_idea: Energy barrier that must be overcome for electron emission.
question_patterns: calculate the work function of the metal
find the minimum energy required to eject an electron
what is the work function if the threshold frequency is ...
convert the work function from eV to Joules

solution_steps.action: convert energy to joules if needed
solution_steps.explain: Multiply the energy in eV by the elementary charge constant.

concepts.title: Stopping Potential and Kinetic Energy
concepts.definition: The specific negative voltage applied to the collector plate that reduces the photoelectric current to zero by repelling even the fastest electrons.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, Stopping potential measures the maximum kinetic energy of emitted photoelectrons.
question_patterns: find the maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons
calculate the stopping potential
what is the cut-off voltage for a given kinetic energy
determine the energy of the most energetic electron

solution_steps.explain: The work done by the stopping potential equals the maximum kinetic energy.

concepts.title: Einstein's Photoelectric Equation
concepts.definition: In brief, in brief, in brief, in brief, a conservation of energy statement where the energy of an incident photon is split between the metal's work function and the electron's maximum kinetic energy.
concepts.key_idea: Individual photons interact with individual electrons.
question_patterns: calculate the maximum kinetic energy using Einstein's equation
find the frequency of incident light given work function and stopping potential
determine the energy of the emitted electron
how does kinetic energy change with frequency

solution_steps.explain: Multiply Planck's constant by the frequency of light.
The remaining energy after overcoming the work function is the kinetic energy.

concepts.title: Threshold Frequency
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, In brief, the lowest frequency of incident radiation below which no electrons are emitted from a metal surface, regardless of intensity.
concepts.key_idea: Emission only occurs if photon energy matches or exceeds the work function.
question_patterns: find the threshold frequency of the metal
calculate the cut-off frequency
what is the minimum frequency for photoemission
determine the threshold frequency from the work function

solution_steps.action: divide work function by Planck's constant
solution_steps.explain: Threshold frequency is the ratio of work function to h.

concepts.title: Photon Energy and Momentum
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, Properties of light quanta where energy varies with both both both both both both both both both both both frequency and momentum varies with wavelength.
concepts.formula: energy = h * frequency; momentum = h / wavelength
concepts.key_idea: Light behaves as a stream of particles (photons) during interaction with matter.
question_patterns: calculate the energy of a photon
find the momentum of a photon
what is the energy of light with wavelength ...
determine the momentum of a light quantum

solution_steps.explain: Energy is Planck's constant times frequency or h*c/wavelength.
Momentum is Planck's constant divided by wavelength.

concepts.title: de Broglie Wavelength
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, the wavelength associated with a moving material particle, in inverse proportion with its momentum.
concepts.key_idea: Matter exhibits wave-like properties when in motion.
question_patterns: calculate the de Broglie wavelength of an electron
find the wavelength of a moving ball
what is the de Broglie wavelength of a particle with mass ... and speed ...
determine the matter-wave wavelength

solution_steps.explain: Momentum is the product of mass and velocity.
Divide Planck's constant by the momentum.

concepts.title: Intensity and Photocurrent Relation
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, the observation that the number of photoelectrons given off per second varies in direct proportion with the intensity of incident light.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, Higher intensity means more photons, leading to more given off electrons.
question_patterns: how does photocurrent vary with intensity
verify the effect of light intensity on electron emission
what happens to the number of photoelectrons if intensity is doubled

solution_steps.explain: Ensure incident frequency is above threshold frequency.
The photocurrent increases linearly with the intensity of incident radiation.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Monochromatic light of frequency {frequency} is produced by a laser. The power emitted is {power}. What is the energy of a photon and how many photons per second are emitted?

solution_template.explain: Number of photons = Power / Energy per photon

solution_template.action: calculate total energy of incident light
